articles.headline: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
articles.description: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win their division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
articles.body:
The top of the Super Bowl odds board continues to tighten as the championship contenders begin to emerge.

The Los Angeles Rams remain the Super Bowl favorites at +670, a significant lengthening from the +500 they had coming into the season. Meanwhile, the 2-0 Buffalo Bills are creeping up on them at +780, an improvement from the +850 they had after winning on Thursday night, despite not playing Sunday.

That's partially because the Baltimore Ravens lost to the long shot New Orleans Saints (80-1), lengthening them slightly from +920 to +950. The Seattle Seahawks (10-1), San Francisco 49ers (12-1), Kansas City Chiefs (13-1), Philadelphia Eagles (16-1) and Cincinnati Bengals (17-1) all improved in the odds with victories on Sunday.

There were also some significant drops on the board, namely the Chicago Bears, who lengthened from 21-1 and 30-1 after losing to the Minnesota Vikings (30-1) and potentially losing superstar quarterback Caleb Williams to a significant injury.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

articles.headline: Early bets for NFL Week 3: Games that drew our attention once odds came out
articles.description: Which Week 3 lines offered immediate value once odds came out? Here are three early bets to track.
articles.body:
With most of Week 2 in the books, we're already looking ahead to Week 3. Which games grabbed our analysts' attention?

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field on Thursday after escaping the New York Jets in OT in Week 2 and are touchdown favorites. The Jets are again underdogs this week on the road against the Detroit Lions.

Also of immediate interest is the matchup between the New England Patriots and Jacksonville Jaguars.

Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado and Eric Moody break down the games share the bets they're backing before potential shifts later in the week.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures.

 Detroit Lions -6.5 vs. New York Jets

Bowen: The Lions need to make defensive corrections. We can all see that, right? But with extra rest/prep off the Thursday night game, I think Detroit builds a game plan to limit Geno Smith and the Jets. Plus, this Detroit offense, which has averaged 31 points per game over the first two weeks of the season, will have answers for the New York defense. Yes, it's a big spread, but it's also one I'm willing to bet for Dan Campbell's team.

 Green Bay Packers -7 vs. Atlanta Falcons

Moody: Green Bay's offensive line has struggled, putting more pressure on Jordan Love and the passing game, but the Packers still rank ninth in passing yards per game. Atlanta's defense has its work cut out, especially with its own offense ranking 29th in total yards and 31st in points per game. The Packers are 9-3 against the spread in their last 12 home games, and I don't see Atlanta scoring enough to keep this close. Give me Green Bay to cover.

 New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars total points UNDER 44.5

Maldonado: The Patriots are at their best when they run the ball, protect Drake Maye and let the defense control things. Though the Jaguars are capable of hitting a few big plays, Trevor Lawrence followed his huge opener with a quiet afternoon in Denver. Neither offense has been reliable enough, and New England is unlikely to invite a faster-paced game on the road. As long as turnovers don't hand out easy touchdowns, this should stay fairly low scoring.

articles.headline: How to bet Giants-Rams on MNF: Analysis, tips and favorite plays
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Giants-Rams on "Monday Night Football."
articles.body:
The New York Giants' offense hummed in its opener and will look to prove it isn't a pretender as the team travels to Los Angeles for another primetime affair.

The revamped Giants regime put together a triumphant debut, besting the division rival Dallas Cowboys by a score of 28-20 in Week 1. Big Blue controlled much of the contest, despite the single-digit differential. Jaxson Dart picked apart Dallas' secondary, managing a career-best completion percentage of 70.3% while throwing for 230 yards and three scores. In addition to his arm, Dart successfully flustered the Cowboys' defensive front with his legs, closing out the contest with 54 rushing yards on 11 attempts (4.9 yards per carry). In classic John Harbaugh-ian fashion, the ground attack remained physical and efficient, with Cam Skattebo leading the charge with 81 rushing yards, a score and an accompanying end zone backflip.

In stark contrast, the Los Angeles Rams repeatedly tripped up, eventually stalling out against a resurgent San Francisco 49ers squad. Snapping a 17-game TD streak, Matthew Stafford appeared particularly disjointed, finishing with a meager 155 passing yards and a dismal 61.2 quarterback rating. The ground game proved more effective, as the tandem of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 95 rushing yards and the team's lone score before being scripted out of the contest. The duo will look to establish pace against Giants DC Dennard Wilson's rejuvenated unit.

Back on home soil and with 10 days to prepare, the Rams have a distinct advantage over the traveling G-Men. Still, with Myles Garrett on IR (knee) and questions swirling around Aaron Donald's return to action and Puka Nacua's health (questionable, groin), the Giants shouldn't be overlooked. Expect Harbaugh to build on the suffocating approach he took in Week 1, focusing on winning the time-of-possession battle via long drives and efficient passing. Meanwhile, Sean McVay should counter by establishing an up-tempo rhythm early, aggressively dispatching Davante Adams and his other available pass catchers downfield.

Betting outlook

Even with Nacua potentialy sitting, both teams have the adequate firepower to put up points. That's why I'm eyeing the total in this clash. Despite a lackluster Week 1, the Rams' dynamic aerial attack should improve, particularly given key injuries to the Giants' secondary. If Los Angeles gets up early, Dart won't hesitate to push the offense while leaning on a healthy-enough Malik Nabers. With Garrett sidelined and Donald likely on a snap count, the sophomore signal-caller figures to be gifted sufficient time to convert, ultimately boosting the combined score toward 50 points.

The market is anticipating a bounce-back effort from the Super Bowl favorites in their first home game of the season. articles.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
articles.description: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces seven active players making their moves among the greats.
articles.body:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns.

This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season.

Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. 

Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald, who un-retired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. 

As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7 all-time. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach top-five all-time territory.

Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.  

But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks were 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research, heading into the seaosn. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982.

If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the all-time list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White. 

As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape

We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season.

Week 2 update

The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the all-time list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded 1 sack over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

Donald (33rd) is set to make his season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants.

Week 1 update

Of all of the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th.

articles.headline: Harry Maguire: Man United didn't take chances against Fulham, paid the price
articles.description: Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
articles.body:
Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

United were fortunate to leave west London with a point after Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal deceived goalkeeper Bernd Leno and denied Alvaro Arbeloa a first Premier League win in charge.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville branded the first 15 minutes of the second half, which culminated in a comical own goal from Lisandro Martínez to put Fulham in front, the worst he had seen in more than 45 years of watching the team play.

United hit a post in the first half through Bruno Fernandes, while Leno produced fine saves from Cunha, Martinez and Bryan Mbeumo.

"We have got to take our chances and take our moments," Maguire said to club media. "When you come away in the Premier League it is tough and you have seen that in the results this year.

"When we had those moments in that first half, they are big moments in the Premier League and you have really got to take them."

Fulham's goal went down against Martinez's name, but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

The result means United have collected their joint fewest number of points after five matches in Premier League history.

Not since the 2014-15 season under Lous van Gaal have United picked up only five points by this stage and Carrick's class of 2026 will spend the extended international break in the bottom half of the table.

The team 11 years ago recovered from their poor start to eventually finish fourth and Maguire believes the current crop can kick on despite more dropped points.

"Our reaction was so much better and positive than it was last week [against Manchester City] and to concede that goal with the week we have had, the boys showed great spirit and great reaction," he said.

"We pushed them right back and the pressure was relentless. We needed a ball to fall or drop for us.

"It was just unfortunate that the goal did not come earlier as we had the momentum to go and win the match."

- Carrick has an impossible job at Man United after transfer failures

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

Cunha's 89th-minute shot hit defender David Affengruber and span cruelly past the wrong-footed Leno, with Fulham just minutes from victory.

It was, however, a muted, lethargic display from Carrick's team, who are now three league matches without a victory.

But Maguire said: "You have got to ignore the noise and really believe and think about what we have done this year, along with what we need to work on and improve on, but we are not far away."

Sept. 21: Monday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The final Monday of the regular season features only three games -- all evening affairs -- beginning at 6:35 p.m. ET with the Toronto Blue Jays visiting the Baltimore Orioles. A few minutes later, the Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals. The San Francisco Giants entertain the Minnesota Twins, closing out the truncated slate, at 9:45 p.m. ET. 

Three teams have clinched a postseason berth in the American League -- all from the East. The Tampa Bay Rays are on the cusp of securing the division, with the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox ticketed to run back their 2025 wild-card matchup in the Bronx.

The Cleveland Guardians lead the Chicago White Sox by one game in the AL Central. The second-place finisher would be in the driver's seat for the final wild card. In the West, the Texas Rangers are one game up on the Houston Astros. The second-place finisher still has an outside chance at the last wild-card spot.

All three National League divisions have been clinched, with the Atlanta Braves ruling the East, the Milwaukee Brewers sitting atop the Central, and the Los Angeles Dodgers having nailed down the West. The Brewers have a two-game lead over the Dodgers for the best record in the Senior Circuit. The seedings for the Wild Card Series could go down to the end, with the Philadelphia Phillies just one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres. The Arizona Diamondbacks have not yet been eliminated, but they're four games behind the Phillies and a lot has to happen for them to extend their season.

The Blue Jays are set to activate Trey Yesavage from the 15-day IL to start tonight's road affair against the Orioles, but they're aiming for only 45-60 pitches from the 23-year-old right-hander. He has been sidelined following meniscus surgery on his right knee and made only one rehab start, recording just two outs in that effort. The rest of the game will be a bullpen affair.

River Ryan is poised to make his first MLB appearance since 2024. He was acquired by the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal deal. The 28-year-old right-hander was shelved by a hamstring injury at the time but recently made two rehab starts for Triple-A Toledo. He'll handle a few innings before tagging in Keider Montero as the primary pitcher.

articles.headline: Mourinho's ref rants overshadow Madrid derby defeat; can Arsenal shrug off heavy loss?
articles.description: Real Madrid lost the derby to Atletico this weekend, but Jose Mourinho's focus was on the refereeing postgame, not the result. Plus: Can Arsenal shake off a deservedly heavy defeat at Brighton?
articles.body:
The last European soccer weekend is in the books before the three-week international break has been and gone, and we have a lot to talk about. We'll begin in LaLiga with the biggest game of the weekend: the Madrid derby. Jose Mourinho is back on the sideline for Real Madrid and we got a game that had a throwback feel, with fouls, a red card and contentious refereeing decisions overshadowing a 2-1 win for Atletico Madrid that ultimately helps Barcelona -- whose 3-1 victory at Sevilla takes them five points clear after just seven games -- most of all.

The big shock in the Premier League was Brighton's masterful 3-0 drubbing of defending champs Arsenal, a game that was as comprehensive as the scoreline suggests. Will Gunners boss Mikel Arteta be able to shake it off quickly and get his team back on track? Elsewhere, we got talking points galore for Inter Milan and Roma (who played out a revealing 2-2 draw), Manchester United (who gutted out a draw at Fulham), Borussia Dortmund (who stayed perfect in the German Bundesliga), Liverpool (another goal for Alexander Isak!), and much, much more.

It's Monday morning, so what better time for some musings? Let's get into it.

- Carrick keen to find Man Utd positives, but there aren't many right now

- VAR review: Why no penalty for Manchester United at Fulham?

- Lindop: Has Isak finally found form at Liverpool?

Madrid derby reopens a familiar can of worms ... but there was also a game played in the middle of it all

And we're back -- back where we once were, and where we really don't want to be, talking about referees, officiating appointments and conspiracies. Back in a world that, according to Jose Mourinho, he had hoped to have left behind when he left LaLiga in 2013. (Evidently he hasn't been watching Real Madrid TV the last couple of years.)

It's a familiar situation. Real Madrid lose. Some big decisions go against them. Mourinho talks about the officiating -- both referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias ("felt the pressure" ... "not an international standard referee and never will be one") and VAR Daniel Jesus Trujillo Suarez ("he has a history with us" ... "he feels no pressure ... or maybe he feels pressure from certain places") -- and we end up not talking about Atletico's win or the fact that Real Madrid are a whopping six points behind league-leading Barcelona even though it's still just September.

Many Madridistas will nod along knowingly and talk about robbery and conspiracies. Many Mourinho-haters will talk about the same old playbook: deflect, deny, disorient. The thing here is that on the two big decisions that Mourinho cited, with the help of two A4 color printouts, he sort of has a point.

VAR correctly intervened to reverse the yellow card shown to Jude Bellingham after a clash with Cristian Romero and cautioned the Argentine instead, but that could easily have been a red. articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Forecaster Playoff Round 2, Week 2: Sept. 21-27
articles.description: Set your lineups for fantasy baseball's final week with our preview featuring pitcher rankings, hitter ratings and schedule observations.
articles.body:
This is it! The final week of the 2026 fantasy baseball season has arrived. If you've made it this far, congratulations! The final seven days should be a wild race to the finish line, both in the real game and in our own leagues.

Week 25 is one of the more balanced weeks on the schedule, with one exception: The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees begin their week-opening series with a Tuesday doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. One of those games makes up their May 23 postponement. The extra game gives both teams a seven-game final week.

All of the other 28 teams play exactly six games -- and 14 of those 28 split those six games evenly between home and the road. This is a "quality over quantity" week when it comes to matchups analysis. Additionally, most teams begin their weeks on Tuesday, as there are only three games scheduled for Monday.

Remember that MLB schedules all games on its final day, Sunday, Sept. 27, to start within a 15 minute window of one another (between 3:05 p.m. and 3:20 p.m. ET). This is by design to try and heighten the drama of real-life playoff races, but it also creates many mad, 3-4 hour dashes to the finish line in fantasy baseball leagues.

Get your popcorn -- I mean, your peanuts and Cracker Jack -- ready!
